der-die-das.webp.prompt:
Photorealistic photograph for a children's learning app (ages 6 to 9): the everyday things used in a short game that a child and an adult play together at home or outside. The things are the subject, not the people.
Natural daylight, soft and friendly, true-to-life colours and proportions, sharp focus on the things, gentle background blur. A real, lived-in but tidy home (kitchen table, floor, hallway, stairs) or a calm street or park, matching the scene.
Show the material ready to play with, as in a calm moment just before or during the game: large, clearly recognisable, close to the camera, few objects. Do NOT arrange things in countable rows or groups and do NOT show an exact number of anything; quantities are loose and natural (a small stack, a bowl, a basket, a handful). Small items (food, buttons, pasta, socks, pegs, cards) are still gathered together in one bowl, basket or loose heap, NOT yet distributed onto plates, places or rows; plates, cups or similar stand empty or stacked.
People: at most a hand, a forearm or a foot at the edge of the picture, cropped, never a face, never a whole person. Skin tones natural and varied. No stereotyped clothing.
Everything must be factually correct and safe: real everyday objects, correct anatomy of hands (five fingers), no knives, no stove, no fire, no small parts in a child's mouth, nothing dangerous.
No text, no letters, no numbers or digits anywhere (also not on dice faces in focus, clocks, books, packaging), no logos, no brands, no watermarks.
Square format (1:1), the things clearly visible and centred, nothing important at the edges, uncluttered composition.

Scene: A short game called „Hier ist der Pulli“ (German instructions below), played at a table at home.
Photograph the things this game is played with, ready to play, as described here (quantities intentionally left open):
Material: einen Korb mit trockener Wäsche
What happens: Legt ein Teil aus dem Korb zusammen. Socken bleiben im Korb. Reicht es weiter und sagt: … … … Wer es nimmt, legt es auf den Stapel und sagt den Satz noch einmal. Klingen eure Sätze verschieden oder fehlt ein Artikel, sagt ihn vor, wer ihn sicher weiß. Dann sprecht ihr den Satz zusammen. Dann tauscht ihr.
